correctness.rationale: The covariance relation converts the site-dependent physical twist into a constant virtual transfer insertion with increment 4π/L. Simplicity of the dominant transfer eigenvalue gives analytic perturbation; SU(2)-invariance of the unique fixed point forces the first derivative to vanish. Thus λ(δ)=1+O(δ²), λ(4π/L)^L=1+O(L⁻¹), while analytic nonzero boundary coefficients contribute only O(L⁻¹). The stated primitive-transfer and boundary-overlap assumptions are explicit.

value.rationale: Open-boundary simulations are common for matrix-product methods, and boundary edge states are precisely where a periodic-boundary diagnostic cannot simply be applied. The theorem gives an exact O(L⁻¹) benchmark for a broad, explicitly parameterized class of symmetric finite-bond MPS, while keeping the general-Hamiltonian open-boundary problem open. This is a structural finite-size statement, not a routine numerical recomputation.
